src/textual/widgets/tabs.py:1-18 imports rich, the events module, the _layout_resolve module, keys, reactive, renderables.opacity, renderables.underline_bar and widget. Nothing in a lower layer imports widgets.
src/textual/renderables/underline_bar.py:1-6 imports only typing and rich, with no textual imports, so the renderable layer stays free of widget dependencies.

Docs registration: docs/reference/tabs.md:1 (::: textual.widgets.tabs.Tabs), identical to reference.diff:1-7.

Action dispatch by naming convention: tabs.py:354 action_range_clicked is matched by app.py:625 (action_{name}) for the 'range_clicked' meta, which is emitted at tabs.py:190 and underline_bar.py:95-101 and extracted at app.py:639.
Key handling: tabs.py:377 async on_key matches the base Widget.on_key contract (widget.py:356, async) and the reference's override pattern (reference.diff:732).
widgets/__init__.py is not changed. The reference does not export Tabs there either (no hunk in reference.diff), so this is not required.
No new packages. tabs.py imports only rich (already a dependency: pyproject.toml:22, rich ^11.2.0), the stdlib modules math and typing, and textual internals.
underline_bar.py imports only typing and rich.
tests use only rich, io, re and pytest, plus the existing tests.utilities.render helper (test_tabs.py:1-13).
Widget state and input handling are in Tabs (tabs.py:220-406): active name and bar position are Reactive fields (tabs.py:253-254), set in __init__ (tabs.py:289-290).
Layout arithmetic is delegated to the existing layout_resolve (tabs.py:161-167).
Click-span construction is in the renderable (tabs.py:182), and UnderlineBar applies it as meta spans after the style spans (underline_bar.py:95-101).
Dimming of inactive labels goes through Opacity (tabs.py:189-191), as the reference does (reference.diff:621-628).

Animation uses the existing Widget.animate BoundAnimator: tabs.py:370-374 calls it with duration and easing, matching the BoundAnimator.__call__ signature (_animator.py:96-113) and the reference (reference.diff:815-822).
Reactive watcher naming watch__active_tab_name (tabs.py:362) uses the framework's watch_<name> mechanism (reactive.py:103-111).
The @click action convention and action_ dispatch (app.py:625, app.py:639) are reused rather than a new event path.

Private _Edge (tabs.py:50-64) duplicates the Edge concept instead of changing the base Edge Protocol (_layout_resolve.py:13-18, not instantiable). The reference changed Edge to a NamedTuple (reference.diff:322-326). The generated objects satisfy the same attribute protocol that layout_resolve reads (_layout_resolve.py:38-76), so this is not a parallel resolver. It is a minor duplication.
TabsRenderable receives only plain values (tabs.py:85-122) and does not depend on the Tabs widget's state or methods.
Click action strings are built in the renderables (tabs.py:190, underline_bar.py:96-100), the same division the reference uses (reference.diff:621-626, 441-445).

Opacity now keeps segment meta (opacity.py:36-41). Rich's Style._add keeps the left operand's meta (checked in a vendored pip copy of rich, not the project's pinned version), so the click action survives dimming.
Shared weakness, not a regression: tab names are interpolated unescaped into the action string (tabs.py:190, underline_bar.py:96-100), as in the reference.
Google-style docstrings with Args/Returns sections, matching the repository (tabs.py:199-203, 326-329, 495-497).
Tests are plain pytest functions using tests.utilities.render (test_tabs.py:1-13; patch.diff:659-704). tests/widgets/__init__.py mirrors the existing tests/renderables/__init__.py.
Sandbox demo uses .css, matching base sandbox/local_styles.css.
Style-only difference: typing Dict/List/Tuple/Mapping (tabs.py:4, underline_bar.py:3) instead of the builtin generics used in base underline_bar.py:20. This does not violate a convention.

Keyboard: arrows tabs.py:400-402; digits 0-9 tabs.py:403-404 with 0 mapping to the 10th tab or the last tab (activate_tab_by_number, tabs.py:345-352, same as reference.diff:804-808); first-character search tabs.py:317-334 and 405-406, case-insensitive and skipping the active tab.

Escape (tabs.py:397-398) removes focus. The reference calls set_focus without await (reference.diff:746-747), so its Escape never runs. The generated code implements the documented intent (reference.diff:733-737), which I count as a fix, not a regression.

Click: inactive labels carry @click (tabs.py:189-190, matching reference.diff:621-626). Bar spans cover the whole tab (tabs.py:182, underline_bar.py:95-101). The reference's cache arithmetic (reference.diff:642-644) produces offset spans; the generated spans match the reference's comment (reference.diff:641, 'the range that can be clicked'). I read this as a reference defect.
Duplicate names: _displayed_labels (tabs.py:67-82) keeps first position and last label, the same as the reference dict semantics (reference.diff:561).
Animation: tabs.py:370-374 (duration, easing) matches reference.diff:815-822. Empty tabs and unknown active tab behave as in the reference (test_tabs.py:51-58, 72-77).

Deviations, not failures: first-character search applies only to single-character keys (tabs.py:405), while the reference applies it to any key string (reference.diff:754-755). UnderlineBar uses no_wrap=True (underline_bar.py:56, 90), which only changes output when the bar is wider than the console; for Tabs the bar width equals options.max_width (tabs.py:135-139), so there is no visible change.
